reason: Do not assume that explicit edge prediction is required to improve HydroGraphNet. First establish whether selective high-zone cell-budget supervision provides a forecasting and local-budget contribution; require edge methods to demonstrate incremental value over that control.

research_identity.primary_problem: HydroGraphNet graph-level mass conservation does not explicitly control high-fidelity local budgets
research_identity.dualfloodgnn_role: optional external same-dataset benchmark after the HydroGraphNet contribution gate passes

ordered_method_gate.question: Does high-zone cell-budget supervision improve high-zone forecasting or local-budget consistency without materially degrading all-domain forecasting?
Does learned physical-edge transport provide incremental forecast, raw local-budget, interpretability, or conservation value beyond the cell-only control?
If edge adds value, does selective edge computation retain that value at lower complete inference cost than full-edge controls?

claim_paths.cell_only_success_edge_no_increment: Selective high-fidelity-zone local budget regularization for HydroGraphNet. Do not claim explicit learned edge transport or strict local conservation at inference.
claim_paths.cell_only_success_edge_increment: HydroGraphNet-based selective physical-edge local conservation, with the edge mechanism and selective-compute efficiency supported by incremental ablation evidence.
claim_paths.cell_only_failure_edge_success: An edge-informed method may proceed only if it independently passes the frozen forecasting, raw local-budget, learned-edge utility, and efficiency gates.
claim_paths.all_local_methods_fail: Retain as negative development evidence; do not claim publication readiness or consume the sealed test for a failed candidate.

dataset_prerequisites.formal_cell_target: Face Flow Period Average divergence plus known precipitation and omitted-boundary source, collapsed to cells without exposing edge values to the model
